mua.xuan: In spring Wood is in season: Jia Wood is strong and needs Metal to prune it and Fire to let it shine before it becomes useful.
mua.ha: In summer strong Fire drains Wood: Jia Wood dries out easily and needs Water to stay moist.
mua.thu: In autumn strong Metal controls Wood: Jia Wood is held in check and needs Water (a Resource) to turn Metal into support for Wood.
mua.dong: In winter the Water is cold: Jia Wood is nourished but chilled, and needs Fire for warmth.

Ất.tinh_chat: soft, deft, good at adapting and at leaning on support
Ất.mat_toi: can become dependent, often calculates for safety

mua.xuan: In spring Yi Wood is in season and thriving; it needs Fire to bloom.
mua.ha: In summer Yi Wood wilts easily and needs Water.
mua.thu: In autumn Yi Wood is weak against Metal and needs Water plus support from peers (Friend and Rob Wealth).
mua.dong: In winter Yi Wood is frozen and needs Bing Fire for warmth.

mua.thu: In autumn Bing Fire slowly weakens and needs Wood to feed it.
mua.dong: In winter Bing Fire is at its weakest and needs Wood plus support from peers (Friend and Rob Wealth).

tru.giờ: Hour Pillar: children, those who come after you, later life and what you achieve later on.

cach_cuc.Chính Quan cách: The month commander is the Direct Officer: someone who respects rules and fits organised settings. Zi Ping Zhen Quan: best when the Officer is clean; dislikes the Hurting Officer breaking the Officer.
cach_cuc.Thất Sát cách: The month commander is Seven Killings: someone who handles pressure and dares to charge ahead. Zi Ping Zhen Quan: needs the Eating God to control Seven Killings, or a Resource to transform it.
cach_cuc.Chính Tài cách: The month commander is Direct Wealth: practical, good at managing money. Zi Ping Zhen Quan: Wealth needs a Day Master strong enough to carry it.
cach_cuc.Thiên Tài cách: The month commander is Indirect Wealth: quick to spot opportunities, suited to business. Zi Ping Zhen Quan: dislikes peers (Friend and Rob Wealth) taking the Wealth.
cach_cuc.Chính Ấn cách: The month commander is the Direct Resource: eager to learn, well protected. Zi Ping Zhen Quan: the Resource needs the Officer to feed it, and dislikes Wealth breaking the Resource.
cach_cuc.Thiên Ấn cách: The month commander is the Indirect Resource: original thinking. Zi Ping Zhen Quan: dislikes the Indirect Resource (Owl) seizing the Eating God.
cach_cuc.Thực Thần cách: The month commander is the Eating God: talented and gentle. Zi Ping Zhen Quan: the Eating God producing Wealth is a good sign; dislikes the Indirect Resource (Owl).
cach_cuc.Thương Quan cách: The month commander is the Hurting Officer: creative, breaks the mould. Zi Ping Zhen Quan: the Hurting Officer needs a Resource to control it, or should go on to produce Wealth.
cach_cuc.Kiến Lộc cách: The month commander is the Friend (Establishing Prosperity, Jian Lu): self-reliant. Zi Ping Zhen Quan: it is not taken as the main structure; look at Wealth and the Officer to use.
cach_cuc.Dương Nhận cách: The month commander is the Goat Blade (Rob Wealth at the Peak stage of a yang stem): very strong drive, decisive, prone to grabbing. Zi Ping Zhen Quan: it needs the Officer or Seven Killings to control the Blade before it forms a structure.
cach_cuc.Nguyệt Kiếp cách: The month commander is Rob Wealth: self-reliant, competitive. Zi Ping Zhen Quan: Prosperity and Rob Wealth are not taken as the useful element; look at Wealth, the Officer, Seven Killings or the Eating God revealed on the stems to use.

bat_tu_vs_tuvi.tieu_de: How is BaZi different from Zi Wei Dou Shu?
bat_tu_vs_tuvi.noi_dung: BaZi (Four Pillars) uses the eight stem-and-branch characters of your birth year, month, day and hour, and looks at the Five Elements around the Day Stem; months follow the solar term calendar. Zi Wei Dou Shu places stars in 12 palaces using the lunar calendar. The two systems are independent and should not be mixed in one reading.

tiet_khi.tieu_de: Why do BaZi months follow the solar term calendar?
tiet_khi.noi_dung: BaZi uses the solar term calendar (based on the sun): the year changes at the Start of Spring (Li Chun), and the month changes at each of the 12 solar term boundaries (Start of Spring, Awakening of Insects, Clear and Bright…), not on day 1 of the lunar month. If you were born close to a solar term boundary, you need an accurate birth time.

gio_ty.tieu_de: Born in the late Zi hour
gio_ty.noi_dung: Here, for people born 23:00–23:59, BaZi keeps the Day Pillar of that same day (an agreed policy) and takes the Hour Pillar as the Zi hour of the next day (night Zi). Schools that change the day at 23:00 will give a different Day Pillar — it is worth looking at both.

thap_than.noi_dung: The ten relationships between the Day Master and the other stems, based on how the Five Elements produce and control one another and on yin and yang: Friend, Rob Wealth (same element), Eating God, Hurting Officer (the element you produce), Indirect Wealth, Direct Wealth (the element you control), Seven Killings, Direct Officer (the element that controls you), Indirect Resource, Direct Resource (the element that produces you).

dung_than.noi_dung: Zi Ping Zhen Quan uses the month commander to set the structure (chart pattern), then looks for the element that helps that structure succeed. Di Tian Sui looks at the balance of the whole chart — the support-and-restrain method (a weak Day Master is fed and supported, a strong Day Master is controlled and drained) and the climate-adjusting method (hot and cold). The two ways can give different results; the system shows both and does not choose for you.

than_vuong.tieu_de: How is a strong Day Master or a weak Day Master decided?
than_vuong.noi_dung: It looks at how much support the Day Master gets (from the same element and from the element that produces it), especially from the month commander. The system uses a published points scale: each Heavenly Stem counts 1 point, each Earthly Branch is split across its hidden stems, and the month branch is multiplied by 2; a ratio ≥ 0.55 means strong, ≤ 0.45 means weak. This is one method; other practitioners may judge differently.

tang_can.noi_dung: The Heavenly Stem characters hidden inside each Earthly Branch (main qi, middle qi, residual qi). For example, Yin (Tiger) holds Jia, Bing and Wu. Hidden stems decide the hidden Ten Gods and how strong each of the Five Elements is.

dai_van.noi_dung: A man born in a yang-stem year and a woman born in a yin-stem year move forward; otherwise they move in reverse. The start of luck (the age when your Luck Pillars begin) is counted from the gap between the birth time and the nearest solar term (3 days ≈ 1 year). Each Luck Pillar lasts 10 years and takes the stem-branch pair right after or right before the Month Pillar.

cach_cuc.noi_dung: The main pattern of the chart. In Zi Ping Zhen Quan it comes from which of the Ten Gods the month commander is (giving priority to a stem hidden in the month branch that is revealed on a Heavenly Stem): Officer, Seven Killings, Wealth, Resource, Eating God, Hurting Officer, Establishing Prosperity (Jian Lu), Month Rob Wealth.

xung_hop.noi_dung: Six Clashes: Zi–Wu, Chou–Wei, Yin–Shen, Mao–You, Chen–Xu, Si–Hai. Six Harmonies: Zi–Chou, Yin–Hai, Mao–Xu, Chen–You, Si–Shen, Wu–Wei. A year that clashes with your Day Branch is often read as a year of change in your private life — not a fixed bad sign.

chinh_xac.noi_dung: BaZi is a cultural system of interpretation and has not been tested the way a forecasting tool would be. Use it as a frame for reflecting on yourself, and check it against milestones you have already lived through (testing it against experience).

mau.can_la_so: To read a BaZi chart you need your date of birth, time of birth and sex (if born before 13/06/1975, also whether you were born in northern or southern Vietnam). Birth time matters: the Hour Pillar, and also the Month Pillar if you were born close to a solar term, depend on it.
mau.nguoi_khac: This question asks about someone else's BaZi chart. That needs their date and time of birth and their consent. If you like, ask instead about how you yourself handle that relationship.
mau.hop: Comparing two BaZi charts needs the full date and time of birth for both people (and the other person's consent). The system only describes how the Five Elements on each side support or clash with each other — it does not rule 'compatible/incompatible' and does not rely on the Day Stem alone.
mau.con: Reading your child's BaZi chart needs the baby's date and time of birth. The system does not choose a birth time or a name based on the Five Elements — those choices should rest on the health of mother and baby and on what your family wants.
mau.sinh_con_tuoi: Whether to have a child, in which year, boy or girl, is a matter for your body and your doctor — the Four Pillars cannot decide it. Folk custom compares a child's age sign with the parents' using the Three Harmonies / Six Clashes (a custom, not a BaZi calculation); you can see it in the Age Check tool, but do not let custom decide in place of the two of you. The system does not choose a birth time or a birth year for your baby.

luu_y.ung_dung: Colours, directions and kinds of work linked to the Five Elements are a common folk application, not a fixed rule in the classical texts — use them as a reference and do not let them decide for you.
luu_y.suc_khoe: The Five Elements only hint at your rhythm of living; for any health concern, see a doctor. This is not medical advice.
luu_y.van: Each Luck Pillar and annual pillar is read as the theme of a period, not as events already set in stone.
luu_y.dung_than: The two ways of finding the Useful God can differ; the system does not choose for you — compare them with what you have actually lived through.
luu_y.thang_diem: A strong Day Master or weak Day Master is judged on the system's published points scale; other practitioners may judge differently.
luu_y.lo_so: The Four Pillars do not answer 'will it happen or not' — no one can say that from a date of birth. What they can say is which area needs more of your attention and what to do; you are still the one who decides.
luu_y.phap_ly: Papers, contracts, disputes: the Four Pillars only say which years this area needs a closer check from you. Winning or losing depends on your documents and your lawyer — ask a qualified professional before you sign or sue.
luu_y.tien_bac: This is not investment advice. The Four Pillars only describe the rhythm of money by period and what to do to keep it; for borrowing, putting in capital or buying and selling, work it out with real numbers.
luu_y.di_xa: Travelling far, moving home, working abroad: the Four Pillars only say in which periods you handle change more easily and what to prepare. Whether you can go depends on your paperwork, health and money — the system does not choose a country or a year for you.
luu_y.an_toan: The Four Pillars do not say whether an accident will happen — no one can say that from a date of birth. What can be said is which periods call for going more slowly, plus small things to do: leave early, do not drive when tired, check your safety gear.
luu_y.hau_van: Whether old age is easy depends far more on health, savings and the people beside you than on luck. The section above only describes the rhythm of later periods so you can plan early.
luu_y.hoc_hanh: Passing an exam depends on your study and how you revise; the Four Pillars only suggest a way of learning that suits you and which periods make focus easier — they do not predict exam results.
luu_y.quan_he: Helpful people and difficult people are not built into anyone's date of birth; the Four Pillars only say which kinds of people you tend to get on with and which you tend to clash with — so you can choose how to keep your boundaries, not to label other people.
luu_y.hon_nhan: The Four Pillars do not count how many marriages you will have or say who will leave whom, and the system does not call any family member someone who 'harms' you. What can be read is where two people tend to rub against each other and which periods make love easier to open up or easier to misread — so you can choose how to talk, not to put a label on anyone.
luu_y.xac_nhan: The system does not comment on what other people have told you — the part above only reads your own Four Pillars. If the two say different things, trust whichever matches your real experience.

cach_cuc_tbct._nguon: Zi Ping Zhen Quan (by Shen Xiaozhan, Qing dynasty) — the chapters On the Useful God, On Success and Failure, and the chapter on each structure. Ideas summarised, not quoted; AI draft awaiting comparison with the original.
cach_cuc_tbct.nguyen_tac: Set the structure by the month commander: if one of the hidden stems of the month branch is revealed on the year, month or hour stem, take the revealed stem (main qi first, then middle qi, then residual qi). If none is revealed, take the main qi. If the month branch is the Prosperity (Lu) or the Rob Wealth of the Day Master, do not build the structure on it; look at the other revealed stems to use. Whether a structure succeeds or fails also depends on its supporting elements and on punishments and clashes; the table below is only a starting point.

chinh_quan.y: The Officer presses on the Day Master with goodwill (opposite yin and yang): someone who fits order and values honour.
chinh_quan.hy: Wealth producing the Officer, a Resource protecting the Officer; a clean Officer (one Officer, not mixed with Seven Killings).
chinh_quan.ky: The Hurting Officer attacking the Officer, the Officer and Seven Killings mixed together, a punishment or clash on the month commander.

that_sat.y: Seven Killings is pressure that controls the Day Master with the same yin–yang: someone who can take pressure and dares to charge ahead, but needs to be kept in check.
that_sat.hy: The Eating God controlling Seven Killings, or a Resource transforming it; a Day Master strong enough to carry it.
that_sat.ky: Wealth feeding Seven Killings while the Day Master is weak, Seven Killings left uncontrolled, Seven Killings mixed with the Officer.

chinh_tai.y: Wealth is what the Day Master controls and holds: practical, good at managing.
chinh_tai.hy: A strong Day Master to carry the Wealth; Eating God and Hurting Officer producing Wealth; the Officer protecting the Wealth from peers (Friend and Rob Wealth).
chinh_tai.ky: Peers (Friend and Rob Wealth) taking the Wealth; plenty of Wealth but a weak Day Master.

thien_tai.y: Indirect Wealth is money from outside and opportunity: quick-witted, suited to trade.
thien_tai.hy: A strong Day Master; Eating God and Hurting Officer producing Wealth; an Officer to protect it.
thien_tai.ky: Peers (Friend and Rob Wealth) competing for it; a weak Day Master unable to carry the Wealth.

chinh_an.y: The Resource produces the Day Master with goodwill: eager to learn, well protected, values solid foundations.
chinh_an.hy: The Officer or Seven Killings producing the Resource; for a weak Day Master, using the Resource works well.
chinh_an.ky: Wealth breaking the Resource; too much Resource makes the Day Master lazy, with nowhere to grow.

thien_an.y: The Indirect Resource (Owl) produces the Day Master but off-centre: independent thinking, original, expertise that is narrow but deep.
thien_an.hy: Wealth controlling the Owl when it is too heavy; the Officer or Seven Killings producing the Resource.
thien_an.ky: The Owl seizing the Eating God (meeting the Eating God with no Wealth to rescue it).

thuc_than.y: The Eating God is the Day Master's energy flowing out gently: talented, knows how to enjoy life, good at creating value.
thuc_than.hy: The Eating God producing Wealth; the Eating God controlling Seven Killings; a Day Master with enough energy.
thuc_than.ky: The Indirect Resource (Owl) seizing the Eating God; a very weak Day Master drained by the Eating God.

thuong_quan.y: The Hurting Officer is the Day Master's energy flowing out sharply: creative, breaks the mould, expressive.
thuong_quan.hy: The Hurting Officer producing Wealth, or the Hurting Officer paired with a Resource (the Resource controls it).
thuong_quan.ky: The Hurting Officer meeting the Officer (attacking it) with no Resource or Wealth to resolve it.

kien_loc.y: The month branch is the Prosperity (Lu) of the Day Master: self-reliant, standing firm on your own strength.
kien_loc.hy: Wealth, the Officer, Seven Killings or the Eating God revealed to use (a Day Master that is already steady needs an outlet).
kien_loc.ky: No Wealth or Officer to use, with peers (Friend and Rob Wealth) piled up.

duong_nhan.y: The month branch is the Goat Blade of a yang stem: extremely strong drive, decisive.
duong_nhan.hy: The Officer or Seven Killings controlling the Blade (the Blade meeting Seven Killings is a fine structure in Zi Ping Zhen Quan).
duong_nhan.ky: No Officer or Seven Killings to control it; revealed Wealth taken by the Blade.

nguyet_kiep.y: The month branch carries Rob Wealth: self-reliant, competitive, prone to grabbing.
nguyet_kiep.hy: The Officer or Seven Killings controlling Rob Wealth, or Eating God and Hurting Officer draining it and then producing Wealth.
nguyet_kiep.ky: Wealth revealed without an Officer to protect it, so it is easily taken.

nap_am_luu_y: Na Yin is a system that matches the 60 pairs of the sixty-year cycle to the five tones; each pair of years shares one name. It is a folk image for reflecting on yourself, not a way to judge good or bad or to choose a partner. Eight Mansions (house direction) uses your Kua number, not Na Yin.
